database_summary: Small delivery/order/payments schema for a marketplace or platform. Core entities are stores, hubs, channels, drivers. Orders, deliveries and payments are large tables holding transaction-level rows (events/measurements) linked by order/delivery/payment id columns. Schema is denormalized around orders referencing store/channel/payment/delivery ids and deliveries referencing drivers. Many numeric metrics on orders are precomputed. Use caution when joining orders -> deliveries/payments because 1-to-many could exist if ids are not unique across those tables in practice (though IDs appear to be aligned by order id columns).

accepted.name: orders_enriched_with_store_channel_hub
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  orders.order_id AS order_id,
  orders.store_id AS store_id,
  orders.channel_id AS channel_id,
  orders.payment_order_id AS payment_order_id,
  orders.delivery_order_id AS delivery_order_id,
  orders.order_status AS order_status,
  orders.order_amount AS order_amount,
  orders.order_delivery_fee AS order_delivery_fee,
  orders.order_delivery_cost AS order_delivery_cost,
  orders.order_created_hour AS order_created_hour,
  orders.order_created_minute AS order_created_minute,
  orders.order_created_day AS order_created_day,
  orders.order_created_month AS order_created_month,
  orders.order_created_year AS order_created_year,
  orders.order_moment_created AS order_moment_created,
  orders.order_moment_accepted AS order_moment_accepted,
  orders.order_moment_ready AS order_moment_ready,
  orders.order_moment_collected AS order_moment_collected,
  orders.order_moment_in_expedition AS order_moment_in_expedition,
  orders.order_moment_delivering AS order_moment_delivering,
  orders.order_moment_delivered AS order_moment_delivered,
  orders.order_moment_finished AS order_moment_finished,
  orders.order_metric_collected_time AS order_metric_collected_time,
  orders.order_metric_paused_time AS order_metric_paused_time,
  orders.order_metric_production_time AS order_metric_production_time,
  orders.order_metric_walking_time AS order_metric_walking_time,
  orders.order_metric_expediton_speed_time AS order_metric_expediton_speed_time,
  orders.order_metric_transit_time AS order_metric_transit_time,
  orders.order_metric_cycle_time AS order_metric_cycle_time,
  stores.store_name AS store_name,
  stores.store_segment AS store_segment,
  stores.store_plan_price AS store_plan_price,
  stores.store_latitude AS store_latitude,
  stores.store_longitude AS store_longitude,
  hubs.hub_id AS hub_id,
  hubs.hub_name AS hub_name,
  hubs.hub_city AS hub_city,
  hubs.hub_state AS hub_state,
  hubs.hub_latitude AS hub_latitude,
  hubs.hub_longitude AS hub_longitude,
  channels.channel_name AS channel_name,
  channels.channel_type AS channel_type
FROM orders
LEFT JOIN stores ON orders.store_id = stores.store_id
LEFT JOIN hubs ON stores.hub_id = hubs.hub_id
LEFT JOIN channels ON orders.channel_id = channels.channel_id
accepted.description: Denormalized order-level relation joining orders to store, channel and hub descriptive attributes. Useful as a starting point for analytics that need store, channel, or hub context for each order (e.g., revenue by store, orders by channel, location-based reporting). Keeps one row per order_id and preserves the original order-level measures and timestamps. | Use for: Revenue, counts and averages by store, channel, hub, date parts; Order lifecycle timing and delivery performance by store or hub; Geo-based or segment-based order distributions

accepted.name: payments_by_order_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment_order_id AS payment_order_id,
  COUNT(payment_id) AS payments_count,
  SUM(payment_amount) AS payments_amount_sum,
  SUM(payment_fee) AS payments_fee_sum,
  MIN(payment_status) AS payment_status_any -- preserves a status value when needed; callers can inspect / filter
FROM payments
GROUP BY payment_order_id
accepted.description: Aggregated payment metrics rolled up to payment_order_id (the order-level payment connector). Returns sums and counts of payments and fees per payment_order_id. Useful to avoid row-multiplication when joining payments to orders and to support questions about total paid amount, total fees, or number of payment events per order. | Use for: Total paid amount, fees or number of payment attempts per order; Join-safe payment summary when combining with orders to compute net revenue per order

accepted.name: deliveries_by_order_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  delivery_order_id AS delivery_order_id,
  COUNT(delivery_id) AS deliveries_count,
  SUM(delivery_distance_meters) AS deliveries_distance_meters_sum,
  AVG(delivery_distance_meters) AS deliveries_distance_meters_avg,
  MIN(delivery_status) AS delivery_status_any
FROM deliveries
GROUP BY delivery_order_id
accepted.description: Aggregated delivery metrics rolled up to delivery_order_id. Provides count of deliveries, total and average delivery distance and a sample delivery_status. Useful to summarize delivery attempts or multi-part deliveries per order and to safely join to orders without multiplying rows. | Use for: Delivery counts and distances per order; Assessing orders with multiple delivery attempts or unusually long distances

accepted.name: orders_with_payment_and_delivery_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id AS order_id,
  o.store_id AS store_id,
  o.channel_id AS channel_id,
  o.payment_order_id AS payment_order_id,
  o.delivery_order_id AS delivery_order_id,
  o.order_status AS order_status,
  o.order_amount AS order_amount,
  p.payments_count AS payments_count,
  p.payments_amount_sum AS payments_amount_sum,
  p.payments_fee_sum AS payments_fee_sum,
  d.deliveries_count AS deliveries_count,
  d.deliveries_distance_meters_sum AS deliveries_distance_meters_sum,
  d.deliveries_distance_meters_avg AS deliveries_distance_meters_avg
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN payments_by_order_agg p ON o.payment_order_id = p.payment_order_id
LEFT JOIN deliveries_by_order_agg d ON o.delivery_order_id = d.delivery_order_id
accepted.description: Order-level relation that joins orders to aggregated payment and delivery summaries (payments_by_order_agg, deliveries_by_order_agg). Use when analyzing orders together with payment totals and delivery aggregates while preventing multiplicative joins from raw payments/deliveries. | Use for: Compute net revenue per order (order_amount minus fees) using aggregated payment fees; Analyze correlation between delivery distance and payment outcomes at the order level

accepted.name: orders_daily_counts_and_amounts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_created_year AS order_created_year,
  order_created_month AS order_created_month,
  order_created_day AS order_created_day,
  COUNT(order_id) AS orders_count,
  SUM(order_amount) AS order_amount_sum,
  SUM(order_delivery_fee) AS order_delivery_fee_sum
FROM orders
GROUP BY
  order_created_year,
  order_created_month,
  order_created_day
accepted.description: Daily aggregated order counts and sums by order_created_year/month/day. Useful for time series of order volume and gross merchandise value (GMV) at the day grain. Keeps date parts as columns so consumers can filter or roll-up as needed. | Use for: Daily trends of order volume and revenue; Weekly/monthly rollups derived from daily aggregates

accepted.name: drivers_with_delivery_stats
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  deliveries.driver_id AS driver_id,
  COUNT(deliveries.delivery_id) AS deliveries_count,
  SUM(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters) AS delivery_distance_meters_sum,
  AVG(deliveries.delivery_distance_meters) AS delivery_distance_meters_avg,
  MIN(deliveries.delivery_status) AS delivery_status_any
FROM deliveries
GROUP BY deliveries.driver_id
accepted.description: Aggregated delivery statistics per driver (driver_id). Returns counts, sum/avg distances and a sample delivery_status. Useful for driver performance, workload, and distance-related analysis. | Use for: Driver workload and average trip distances; Identifying drivers with many deliveries or outlier distance patterns

accepted.name: store_rank_by_order_amount
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.store_id AS store_id,
  s.store_name AS store_name,
  s.store_segment AS store_segment,
  COALESCE(SUM(o.order_amount), 0) AS store_order_amount_sum,
  COALESCE(COUNT(o.order_id), 0) AS store_orders_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(o.order_amount),0) DESC) AS store_rank
FROM stores s
LEFT JOIN orders o ON s.store_id = o.store_id
GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name, s.store_segment
accepted.description: Rank stores by total order_amount using a window function. Produces one row per store with aggregated measures and a rank (1 = highest total order_amount). Useful as a basis for top-N store queries by adding WHERE store_rank <= K downstream. | Use for: Top-N stores by GMV or order count; Tiering stores by revenue rank for segmentation
